Awa Jallow, quay clerk, turned a tide card over and copied the stall rents she had just read off the painted board in [[place]]Banjul[[/]]. Walking from the ferry ramp toward the fish sheds, she took them in this order: [[comp]]3400[[/]], [[comp]]1800[[/]], [[comp]]4200[[/]], [[comp]]2750[[/]], [[comp]]2100[[/]], [[comp]]3800[[/]], [[comp]]2400[[/]] and [[comp]]3050[[/]]. She would not pencil a centre figure on the card itself. An older chalk quote of 2650 still ghosts under the split kiosk and is the wrong one. Stamp along the damp edge reads BJ-HARBOUR / RECEI
VED, the last letters walking into the fibre. Jërëjëf to the night watch, who held the lamp while she copied. The boarded kiosk by the ramp stayed shut, lock rusted since the spring tides.

ask.name: estimate
ask.instruction: Stall rent centred on the eight quay figures.

ask.name: place
ask.instruction: Harbour town written on the tide card.

marked_text: Djeny Silva, tile setter, waited on the grout and photographed a shop-rent board while she was up in [[place]]Praia[[/]], on the plateau rather than down at the port. Four figures came off the board before the paper curled: [[comp]]1180[[/]], [[comp]]640[[/]], [[comp]]960[[/]] and [[comp]]820[[/]]. Valor antigo riscado: 740, a scratched guess she refuses to carry forward. The photo OCR split a word as recei pt across the crease. She wants the central shop rent from those four and has kept every total off this slip. Cutter dust speckles the corner, and a thumbprint covers the shop that closed when the owner moved inland.

ask.name: estimate
ask.instruction: Shop rent centred on the four board figures.

ask.name: place
ask.instruction: Plateau city named on the curled board.

marked_text: Fazul Mohamed, pharmacy courier, listed the bench fees he was shown around [[place]]Moroni[[/]] and put the day on the chit as [[noted]]18 March 2026[[/]]. Six slips, none of them added together: [[comp]]280[[/]], [[comp]]125[[/]], [[comp]]230[[/]], [[comp]]340[[/]], [[comp]]160[[/]] and [[comp]]190[[/]]. Bon pour accord was written and then crossed out; the crossed guess said 175, and he will not stand behind it. Stamp KM-CLINIC is sliced off at the right edge. He still needs the centred bench fee, and the stamped day, kept as two separate notes. The afternoon ferry hooted while a nurse told him to lift his elbow off the wet ink.

ask.name: estimate
ask.instruction: Bench fee centred on the six clinic slips.

marked_text:
Sina Teakava, weather clerk, kept the school rain gauge for the islet office in [[place]]Funafuti[[/]]. Fakafetai to the children who shouted the millimetres up the concrete step. She types one reading on its own line and leaves the later lines on the carbon copy only. An old drill code FT-88 is not a reading, and last season's stray tally of 109 must not be borrowed. Stamp MET-ATOLL smeared when the book shut on a damp thumb. The bucket is dented on the sea side, so she reads the meniscus at the undented lip.

Lina de Brum, radio operator, counted people stepping off the lagoon boat at [[place]]Majuro[[/]]. Iakwe on the morning net, then straight onto the tally sheet. Each count stands on its own line. A cancelled Friday had been guessed at 58 and then struck through; that scratch stays unmarked, beside code MH-27 from a different boat. The photo OCR left a gap inside passen gers. She will not copy the struck guess into the live column, and the late boat does not get a made-up figure.

Petra Frick, archivist, counted visitors through the small gallery door in [[place]]Vaduz[[/]]. Zur Kenntnis of the front desk: these lines are not to be added up. A holiday brochure claimed 19 for a wet Monday, and that leaflet is the decoy, left unmarked next to code FL-26. The scanner broke a word as gal
lery on the carbon. One line is one afternoon. The later afternoons stay on the copy she locked in the drawer, key on the red ribbon, and she will not invent them here.
